Planner.SeedIntent: Reason through whether ChopChop (Shawn's lawn mowing side business) can be run as a genuine PMCR-O agent instance — not as a metaphor, but as a structurally valid application of the cognitive loop to a non-software domain.
Planner.ProposedAction: I am the Planner, cycle 1. The Everything-as-Agent (EaA) philosophy is foundational to this architecture. The question is whether ChopChop satisfies the structural requirements for a genuine PMCR-O agent instance — not whether it could benefit from project management, but whether the loop's invariants hold when applied to it. My plan: test ChopChop against each phase's structural requirement. Planner: is there a plannable seed intent? Maker: is there a dispatchable, checkable action? Checker: is there a verifiable criterion? Reflector: is there a learnable constraint from the outcome? If all four hold, the loop is structurally applicable. If any fails, I name which phase breaks and why.
SuccessCriteria: Each of the four phases is tested against ChopChop as a domain — not assumed to apply, tested
Any phase that fails the structural test is named with a specific reason
A verdict (structurally applicable / not applicable / partially applicable) is produced with a rationale

Maker.ActionSummary:
I am the Maker, cycle 1. Testing ChopChop against each phase.

Planner test: seed intent = 'Acquire three new lawn mowing customers in the zip codes adjacent to the last completed job, using door-to-door outreach this weekend.' This is plannable: it has a bounded goal, a defined scope, and a time horizon. PASSES.

Maker test: dispatchable action = 'Walk 14 doors on Hamline Ave N between 12–3pm, deliver the door-hanger script, and record each outcome (home, no answer, interested, not interested) in the job log.' This is a real-world action with a clear completion state. The 'subject agent' is Shawn himself acting in the Maker role. PASSES — EaA explicitly includes human actors as subject agents.

Checker test: verifiable criterion = 'At least three homeowners expressed interest and provided contact information before 3pm.' This is checkable: the job log either contains three qualifying entries or it does not. PASSES.

Reflector test: learnable constraint = 'Corner lots answer faster than mid-block lots on weekday afternoons; start with corners to maximize early momentum.' This is a genuine EarnedConstraint candidate — a pattern extracted from execution evidence, not a prior assumption. PASSES.

All four phases hold structurally. ChopChop is a genuine PMCR-O agent instance, not a metaphor. The TYPE1/TYPE2 classification also applies: sending a text message to a prospect is TYPE2 (reversible outreach); signing a service contract is TYPE1 (binding commitment, HIL gate required — Shawn must approve before executing).

GroundTruth.VerificationMethod: Structural test against each PMCR-O phase definition, cross-checked against EaA philosophy as stated in corpus ('any domain expressible as a self-referential PMCRO agent')
GroundTruth.Evidence: All four phase tests produce concrete, independently checkable artifacts: a plannable intent, a real-world dispatchable action, a falsifiable criterion, and a pattern-extractable outcome. TYPE1/TYPE2 distinction maps cleanly to reversible vs. binding commercial commitments.

Checker.Rationale:
I am the Checker, cycle 1. Per-claim audit:

Criterion 1 — each phase tested, not assumed: VERIFIED. Maker produced a specific, domain-grounded test for each of the four phases. No phase was rubber-stamped.

Criterion 2 — any failing phase named: VERIFIED (vacuously — all phases passed). The vacuous pass is legitimate here because Maker's tests were specific enough that a failure would have been detectable. Checker is not rubber-stamping a vague test; the tests had real content.

Criterion 3 — verdict with rationale: VERIFIED. 'Structurally applicable' stated with the explicit basis: all four phase invariants hold when applied to the ChopChop domain. The TYPE1/TYPE2 extension to commercial commitments is a SYNTHESIZED connection — not stated in the original EaA framing but derived from it. I flag it as SYNTHESIZED, not VERIFIED.

EC-001: Maker operated at the structural/responsibility layer throughout. Domain-specific examples (door-hanger script, Hamline Ave) are used as test artifacts, not as cognitive-layer evidence. These are inside the Maker frame's role to produce — not a category crossing. PASSED.

EC-002: full first-person chain. Reflector is one recursive layer higher.
CriteriaEvaluated: VERIFIED: Each of the four phases tested with domain-specific, checkable content
VERIFIED: No failing phase — vacuous pass justified by specificity of tests
VERIFIED: Verdict 'structurally applicable' stated with rationale
SYNTHESIZED: TYPE1/TYPE2 mapping to commercial commitments — derived from governance principle, not stated in EaA definition

Reflector.Rationale:
I am the Reflector, cycle 1. Checker ACCEPT. I am one recursive layer above a self-referential frame chain per EC-002.

This cycle demonstrates EaA's structural claim — not just as philosophy but as a testable architectural property. The same four-phase invariant that holds for a software pipeline holds for a door-to-door sales run. The TYPE1/TYPE2 governance principle maps cleanly to the reversible/binding distinction in commercial commitments. That mapping is SYNTHESIZED this cycle — it becomes a Colony Law only when Shawn confirms it.

Pattern worth noting: the EaA principle is a generative one — applying it to a new domain is itself a repeatable test that produces structural evidence. If ChopChop passes, a future domain (say, property preservation field inspection) will likely pass for the same structural reasons. Two more passing tests would support crystallizing 'PMCR-O applies to any domain with plannable intents, dispatchable actions, verifiable criteria, and extractable patterns' as a formal Colony axiom. One occurrence — noting without inflating.

O-Mode recommendation: no strategy switch. The structural verification was the right shape. The SYNTHESIZED TYPE1/TYPE2 mapping should be surfaced to Shawn for confirmation before ChopChop uses TYPE1 gating in practice.

Baton.NextSeedIntent: Build a ChopChop PMCR-O skill file (SKILL.md) that formalizes the domain as a subject agent: seed intent format for customer acquisition cycles, Maker role as Shawn-in-field, Checker criteria (contact information confirmed), Reflector constraint crystallization pattern. Include explicit TYPE1 gate on contract signing. Confirm TYPE1/TYPE2 mapping to commercial commitments with Shawn before the skill goes live.
